acts.9.p1.b1.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest

acts.9.p1.b2.text: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.

acts.9.p1.b3.text: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey,

acts.9.p1.b4.text: … suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

acts.9.p2.b1.text: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him,

acts.9.p3.b2.text: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,”

acts.9.p3.b3.text: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

acts.9.p3.b4.text: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.

acts.9.p4.b1.text: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing.

acts.9.p4.b2.text: So they led him by the hand into Damascus.

acts.9.p4.b3.text: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything.

acts.9.p5.b1.text: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias.

acts.9.p5.b4.text: “Get up!” … “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.

acts.9.p6.b1.text: “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.

acts.9.p6.b2.text: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”

acts.9.p6.b3.text: “Go!” … “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.

acts.9.p6.b4.text: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”

acts.9.p7.b1.text: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul.

acts.9.p7.b3.text: “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me

acts.9.p7.b4.text: so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

acts.9.p8.b1.text: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored.

acts.9.p8.b2.text: He got up and was baptized,

acts.9.p8.b3.text: and after taking some food, he regained his strength.

acts.9.p9.b1.text: And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.

acts.9.p9.b2.text: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”

acts.9.p9.b3.text: “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name?

acts.9.p9.b4.text: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.

acts.9.p10.b1.text: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

acts.9.p10.b2.text: Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.

acts.9.p10.b3.text: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.

acts.9.p11.b1.text: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

acts.9.p11.b2.text: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles

acts.9.p11.b3.text: and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus,

acts.9.p12.b1.text: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

acts.9.p12.b2.text: … but they tried to kill him.

acts.9.p12.b3.text: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

acts.9.p12.b4.text: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.

acts.9.p13.b1.text: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.

acts.9.p13.b2.text: There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.

acts.9.p13.b3.text: “Aeneas,” … “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.”

acts.9.p13.b4.text: Immediately Aeneas got up, and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

acts.9.p14.b1.text: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha … who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.

acts.9.p14.b2.text: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.

acts.9.p14.b3.text: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him,

acts.9.p15.b1.text: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room.

acts.9.p15.b2.text: All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.

acts.9.p16.b1.text: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed,

acts.9.p16.b3.text: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.

acts.9.p16.b4.text: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
